heroHeadline: DGMO Talks and Drone Intercepts on Day 366: India-Pakistan Ceasefire Holds Amid Active Border Tensions and Competing Victory Narratives
heroSubtitle: May 12, 2026: India and Pakistan DGMOs held hotline talks reaffirming no-firing commitments and discussing forward troop reductions — the same evening Indian air defences intercepted suspected Pakistani drones in the Samba sector (International Border) and Rajouri/Poonch (LOC). India's MEA issued a sharp rebuke to China for providing technical support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor, warning 'responsible countries must reflect on consequences.' Pakistan's National Assembly unanimously passed a resolution honouring its armed forces, the legislative capstone of a week-long Marka-e-Haq anniversary commemoration. The bilateral freeze remains total: mutual airspace closure through May 24, Indus Waters Treaty suspended, all direct trade halted, no ambassadors exchanged. The ceasefire line is holding but drone intrusions and LOC skirmishes continue amid zero diplomatic normalization.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
